target_customer: Web and mobile app developers who want a hosted realtime backend without running servers
problem: Developers building realtime apps had to build and scale their own sync servers and backends. Firebase gave them a hosted realtime database and API.
business_model: Usage-tiered developer platform subscription (hosted realtime database), later a free tier inside Google Cloud
product_category: Backend as a service, realtime database, developer platform

founders.name: James Tamplin
previous_startups: Envolve (chat API, founded 2011 with Andrew Lee, split into Firebase)
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as founder and CEO; later cofounded CovidActNow.org.

founders.name: Andrew Lee
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as founder. Education and prior employers not found in sources opened.

competitors.name: Parse
competitors.what: Hosted backend for mobile apps with JSON data store

competitors.name: StackMob
competitors.what: Hosted backend with API creation, push notifications and analytics

competitors.name: Kinvey
competitors.what: Hosted mobile backend with collection based data model

technical_complexity.rationale: Low latency realtime sync across clients with scaling, security rules and client libraries is hard distributed systems work for a two person team.

defensibility.rationale: Apps built on the realtime API and data model are costly to move; realtime out of the box was an edge over Parse and Kinvey per later comparisons.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Google acquired Firebase in October 2014 and later made it an umbrella brand for its mobile developer products.

market_need_then: Mobile and realtime apps were growing quickly and customers used the chat product for non-chat data sync, which showed demand for a hosted realtime database. Several backend as a service firms were funded in 2011 and 2012.

branding.domain_note: Used firebase.com during independence; moved to firebase.google.com after the acquisition.

identity.logo: Stylized flame mark made of overlapping triangular shapes, refined in 2016 per a logo site
identity.visual_style: Developer tooling aesthetic with flame iconography

branding.brand_signature: The flame mark and the name later reused as Google's umbrella brand for app developer products
branding.community_and_virality: Large developer community; Google later renamed products such as Cloud Messaging to Firebase Cloud Messaging.

brand_strength.rationale: Became an umbrella developer brand across Google, which suggests brand equity, though sources do not state the brand drove the 2014 deal.

pivots.why: Customers used the chat system to sync non-chat app data, so founders split the realtime layer into its own company

outcome_analysis: Firebase came from pivoting the Envolve chat API once customers used it to sync app data, launched in April 2012, raised about 1.1 million dollars of seed and a 5.6 million dollar Series A in 2013, then sold to Google in October 2014 for an undisclosed price. It grew into Google's mobile developer platform brand, a strong outcome driven by a successful pivot into a hot backend market.
notes: Company site firebase.com now serves Google's firebase.google.com, which does not mention history.
